end.summary:
Ira practised reading position-time and velocity-time graphs.
They used slope of an x-t graph to find velocity and identify motion stories.
They used slope of a v-t graph to find acceleration and area under it to find displacement.
They correctly calculated 3 m/s² and 120 m in the examples.
end.parentNote: Ira practised connecting graph features with motion: x-t slope gives velocity, v-t slope gives acceleration, and v-t area gives displacement. They explained their answers with examples, including why a horizontal x-t line means the object is stationary. A brief mix-up about a horizontal v-t line was corrected within the lesson: it shows constant velocity, while a line on the time axis shows zero velocity. At home, ask Ira to describe one everyday motion using both an x-t and a v-t graph.
